# camera (device class)

> USB cameras, including a laptop's built-in webcam — parked when nobody is using them

A camera on USB, which in practice means a UVC webcam: the laptop's built-in one, or one plugged in. The kernel drives it with uvcvideo and presents it as /dev/videoN.

## Devices in this class

- [sunplus-integrated-webcam-fhd](sunplus-integrated-webcam-fhd.md)

## Shared setup

Nothing to install. Park and wake are `hammunition hardware park camera` and `hammunition hardware wake camera`, through the same helper the tray uses.

## Power control

This device can be parked and woken. Method: `usb_deauthorize`.

A parked USB camera is unconfigured, not unpowered at the port: uvcvideo drops /dev/videoN and the port is only allowed to suspend, so the camera stops being a camera to every program. This does not cut its supply, and it is not a hardware privacy switch: a camera is as unusable while parked as software can make it, which is a statement about the kernel's view, not a guarantee about the module. Nothing needs quieting first. Parking has not been run on a camera here (unmeasured).

See [device power control](power-control.md) for what parking does to a machine, how to inspect it and how to reverse it.
